actions.title: Obtain Daily Weight
actions.prompt: You are obtaining the patient’s current daily weight. Which method is the best and most reliable way to obtain an accurate weight that can be compared to their previous/future weights?
items: Weigh the patient wearing similar clothing, with shoes removed, and document the weight using the same type of scale used previously whenever possible.
Ask the patient what their average daily weight was at home and document that value.
Weigh the patient while they are seated and subtract the estimate of the weight of any urine or stool if they have not recently voided.
Record the last documented weight from the medical record if the patient reports they feel about the same as usual.
actions.correct: Weigh the patient wearing similar clothing, with shoes removed, and document the weight using the same type of scale used previously whenever possible.
actions.resultName: Current weight: 182 lbs (83 kg)

actions.title: Perform Focused Cardiovascular Assessment #1
actions.prompt: Before initiating any interventions for a hospitalized patient with worsening shortness of breath, which set of assessment findings best represents a focused cardiovascular assessment the nurse should complete?
items: Assess heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, presence of peripheral edema, skin temperature and color, capillary refill, and ask about chest discomfort or pressure.
Assess lung sounds, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, use of accessory muscles, and ability to speak in full sentences.
Review the patient’s medication administration record, verify IV access patency, prepare oxygen equipment, and apply continuous pulse oximetry.
Obtain a full neurological exam, assess pupil response, check bowel sounds, and review the patient’s most recent laboratory results.
actions.correct: Assess heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, presence of peripheral edema, skin temperature and color, capillary refill, and ask about chest discomfort or pressure.
actions.resultName: Heart rate is tachycardic and regular. Blood pressure is elevated. Mild bilateral ankle edema (1+) is present. Skin is warm with capillary refill under 3 seconds.

actions.title: Perform Focused Cardiovascular Reassessment #2
actions.prompt: After initiating nursing interventions for a hospitalized patient with shortness of breath (such as positioning and supplemental oxygen), which assessment findings are most important for the nurse to include when performing a focused cardiovascular reassessment?
items: Reassess heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, peripheral edema, skin color and temperature, capillary refill, and ask whether chest discomfort or heaviness has improved.
Repeat lung sounds, count respiratory rate, reassess oxygen saturation, and evaluate the patient’s ability to speak in full sentences.
Review laboratory results, confirm IV access patency, and prepare to administer ordered medications.
Complete a full head‑to‑toe assessment, including neurological status, bowel sounds, and urinary output trends.
actions.correct: Reassess heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, peripheral edema, skin color and temperature, capillary refill, and ask whether chest discomfort or heaviness has improved.
actions.resultName: Heart rate decreased and remains regular. Blood pressure improves slightly. Chest heaviness improved. Skin remains warm with adequate capillary refill, and mild ankle edema persists without acute worsening.

actions.title: Perform Focused Respiratory Assessment #1
actions.prompt: Before providing interventions for a hospitalized patient with worsening shortness of breath, which findings should the nurse include in a focused respiratory assessment?
items: Assess respiratory rate and pattern, work of breathing and use of accessory muscles, ability to speak in full sentences, lung sounds, oxygen saturation, cough presence and character, and patient positioning tolerance.
Assess heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, peripheral edema, skin temperature, capillary refill, and ask about chest discomfort.
Apply supplemental oxygen, raise the head of the bed, coach slow breathing, and reassess oxygen saturation.
Review recent laboratory results, confirm IV access, prepare oxygen equipment, and notify the provider of the patient’s condition.
actions.correct: Assess respiratory rate and pattern, work of breathing and use of accessory muscles, ability to speak in full sentences, lung sounds, oxygen saturation, cough presence and character, and patient positioning tolerance.
actions.resultName: Respiratory rate is tachypneic with increased effort and mild accessory muscle use. The patient speaks in short phrases. Oxygen saturation is decreased on room air. Bibasilar crackles and diminished aeration are present at the lung bases. The patient reports worse breathing when lying flat and prefers to sit upright.

actions.title: Perform Focused Respiratory Reassessment #2
actions.prompt: After positioning the patient upright and initiating supplemental oxygen for worsening shortness of breath, which findings are most important for the nurse to include when performing a focused respiratory reassessment?
items: Reassess respiratory rate and pattern, work of breathing and accessory muscle use, oxygen saturation and oxygen delivery device settings, lung sounds, ability to speak in full sentences, and the patient’s reported ease of breathing.
Reassess heart rate and rhythm, blood pressure, peripheral edema, skin temperature, capillary refill, and presence of chest discomfort.
Review laboratory results, confirm IV access patency, prepare to administer provider‑ordered medications, and update the medication administration record.
Complete a full head‑to‑toe assessment, including neurological status, bowel sounds, urinary output, and skin integrity.
actions.correct: Reassess respiratory rate and pattern, work of breathing and accessory muscle use, oxygen saturation and oxygen delivery device settings, lung sounds, ability to speak in full sentences, and the patient’s reported ease of breathing.
actions.resultName: Respiratory rate decreased. Work of breathing and accessory muscle use improved. The patient speaks in fuller sentences. Oxygen saturation improved on supplemental oxygen. Bibasilar crackles remain, but no new adventitious sounds are present. Patient remains comfortable upright.

actions.title: Perform Patient Repositioning - High Fowler’s – HOB Elevated 60-90 Degrees
actions.prompt: Arrange the following steps in chronological order for how they should be performed to place the patient into a High-Fowler’s position with the head of bed (HOB) elevated 60-90 degrees.
items: Explain the positioning change and obtain the patient’s agreement.
Raise the head of the bed to approximately 60-90 degrees while supporting alignment and comfort.
Use pillows as needed to support the arms and upper body.
Confirm that the patient is comfortable and breathing more easily.
actions.resultName: The patient is repositioned and appears to be breathing easier.

actions.title: Perform Patient Repositioning – Semi-Fowler’s – HOB Elevated to 30 Degrees
actions.prompt: Arrange the following steps in chronological order for how they should be performed to place the patient into a Semi-Fowler’s position with the head of bed (HOB) elevated 30-45 degrees.
items: Explain the positioning change and obtain the patient’s agreement.
Raise the head of the bed to approximately 30-45 degrees while supporting alignment and comfort.
Use pillows as needed to support the arms and upper body.
Confirm that the patient is comfortable and breathing more easily.
actions.resultName: The patient is repositioned and breathing appears unchanged.

actions.title: Provide Patient Education
actions.prompt: A hospitalized patient with an acute exacerbation of heart failure is short of breath and has just been placed on supplemental oxygen. Which patient education is most appropriate for the nurse to provide at this time?
items: Explain in simple terms that sitting upright and using oxygen will help make breathing easier, encourage slow, controlled breathing, and instruct the patient to use the call light if breathing worsens or chest discomfort occurs.
Provide detailed education about heart failure pathophysiology, review long‑term medication management, and discuss dietary sodium limits and daily weight monitoring.
Reassure the patient that the provider will decide what to do next and instruct the patient to rest quietly without asking questions until testing is complete.
Teach the patient how to adjust the oxygen flow rate independently and explain when to increase the amount of oxygen if shortness of breath returns.
actions.correct: Explain in simple terms that sitting upright and using oxygen will help make breathing easier, encourage slow, controlled breathing, and instruct the patient to use the call light if breathing worsens or chest discomfort occurs.
actions.resultName: Patient noted to frequently nod head during conversation and maintained good eye contact.

sbar.situation:
The date and time of this simulated clinical encounter is: July 22, 09:00.
You are receiving report on Aisha Rahimi, a 50-year-old woman admitted to the inpatient medical-surgical unit earlier today. Over the past hour, she has developed increased shortness of breath and appears more fatigued.
sbar.background: Aisha has heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and hypertension. She was admitted for monitoring after two days of worsening shortness of breath. She is currently on room air and has been resting in bed. No acute procedure has been performed today.
sbar.assessment: At report, Aisha appears mildly anxious and says she is more short of breath than earlier. She is speaking in short phrases. Lung sounds, respiratory effort, and current oxygen saturation have not yet been reassessed since the change in symptoms.
sbar.recommendation: Promptly complete focused respiratory and cardiovascular assessments, obtain vital signs including pulse oximetry, position the patient to support breathing, follow active oxygen and monitoring orders, reassess the response, and communicate and document concerning findings.

orders.title: Chest X-Ray (CXR)
orders.instructions: Two-view chest radiograph obtained for evaluation of shortness of breath and possible pulmonary congestion.

orders.instructions: Obtain a 12-lead ECG for evaluation of tachycardia and chest heaviness.

orders.title: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP)
orders.instructions: B-type natriuretic peptide collected for evaluation of possible heart failure exacerbation.

orders.title: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP)
orders.instructions: Basic metabolic panel collected for evaluation of electrolytes and renal function.

orders.title: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
orders.instructions: Complete blood count collected as part of the evaluation for worsening shortness of breath.

orders.title: High-Sensitivity Troponin
orders.instructions: High-sensitivity troponin collected for evaluation of chest heaviness and possible myocardial injury.

orders.title: Vital Signs Every 4 Hours
orders.instructions: Obtain and document temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, pain, and oxygen saturation every 4 hours and as needed for changes in condition.

orders.title: Oxygen Protocol
orders.instructions: As needed, apply oxygen to maintain saturation >94%, start at 2 LPM via Nasal Cannula and titrate by 0.5 LPM every 5 minutes until target saturation is achieved

orders.title: Activity as Tolerated
orders.instructions: Activity as tolerated. Limit exertion during acute dyspnea and assist with repositioning or mobility as needed. Keep head of bed (HOB) elevated to reduce dyspnea.

orders.title: Intake and Output Monitoring
orders.instructions: Measure and document oral intake and urine output each shift. Report decreasing output or signs of worsening fluid retention.

orders.title: Daily Weights
orders.instructions: Obtain daily weight at the same time each morning using the same scale and similar clothing, before breakfast when possible.

orders.title: Low-Sodium Diet with Fluid Restriction
orders.instructions: Maintain a sodium-restricted diet (<1500 mg sodium/day) with 2000 mL/day fluid restriction

orders.title: Cardiac Telemetry
orders.instructions: Initiate and maintain cardiac telemetry. Notify the provider of new dysrhythmia or clinically significant rate change.

orders.title: Continuous Pulse Oximetry
orders.instructions: Initiate and maintain continuous pulse oximetry and monitor the trend.

orders.title: Respiratory Therapy Evaluation and Treatment
orders.instructions: Respiratory therapy to evaluate oxygen delivery, breathing pattern, and need for additional respiratory support according to current findings and provider direction.

additionalEquipment: Hand hygiene supplies; adjustable hospital bed with linens; extra pillows; stethoscope; blood pressure cuff/monitor; pulse oximeter; thermometer; oxygen source; oxygen flowmeter; nasal cannula

Place the oxygen source, flowmeter, nasal cannula, pulse oximeter, blood pressure equipment, stethoscope, and extra pillows within the room and visible to the learner.

teamCommunication.prompt: You are the nurse caring for this patient. Provide a brief, concise, high-quality SBAR report to the provider about the patient’s declining oxygenation and response to nursing interventions.
teamCommunication.passMessage: Thank you for the clear update. I will place orders. Let me know if her oxygen needs increase, chest discomfort worsens, or respiratory distress returns.
teamCommunication.failMessage: Try again using SBAR. Include the current oxygen saturation and respiratory rate, the focused respiratory and cardiovascular findings, what you did, how the patient responded, and what you are requesting.
